intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Bethesda that starts with a rendering, not a guess
paragraphs: Boss Design Center handles kitchen remodeling in Bethesda from its showroom at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue. It is a design-build firm, so the designer who draws your kitchen stays involved until the job is done. Before any wall comes down, you see a photorealistic 3D rendering of the finished room.

Every tile, cabinet and fixture is picked before construction starts, which lets the firm write a fixed-rate contract with no allowances. Its own kitchen projects run $80,000 to $250,000. You can touch cabinet doors, counters and tile in person at the Bethesda showroom or the McLean design campus on Chain Bridge Road. One Google reviewer wrote that Talha and his crew get things done correctly the first time.

services.h2: What the Boss team designs and builds

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Traditional, transitional, modern, coastal and French-inspired kitchens, plus German-made cabinetry with handleless and designer-series options. Structural changes are welcome, as the firm's Arlington kitchen project shows. You choose cabinets, counters, backsplash and hardware in the showroom, not from catalog photos.

image.alt: Arlington, VA kitchen remodel with light oak cabinets, purple-veined stone counters, a woven rattan pendant and a breakfast table by French doors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Small baths, modern and classic baths, and primary suites. You see the room in a 3D rendering and revise it until it is right, then pick tile, vanities and fixtures in person. Your project manager runs the daily work and meets with you every week.

image.alt: Bethesda, MD bathroom on Edgemoor Lane with ribbed wood-look wall tile, a frameless glass shower, heated towel rail and floating oak vanity

items.name: Whole Home Remodeling
items.blurb: For growing families, empty nesters, historic houses and new homes that need to feel like yours. One design idea carries through every room, and a single accountable team handles the kitchen, the baths, the basement and the spaces in between.

image.alt: Reston, VA whole house remodel with a two-story great room, exposed timber ceiling beams, a loft railing and an iron ring chandelier

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: A dark lower level that feels more like a root cellar can become real living space. The crew opens walls, checks what is behind them and handles the permits, then finishes the basement under the same fixed-rate contract and weekly updates as a kitchen.

image.alt: Boss Design crew member checking an opened basement wall at the start of a basement finishing project

items.name: Aging-in-Place Remodeling
items.blurb: Certified Aging-in-Place Specialists on staff plan barrier-free showers, grab bars that look like fixtures, comfort-height toilets, pull-out shelving and wider doorways. The goal is a safer home with no institutional look, and it starts with a free home assessment.

image.alt: McLean, VA bathroom with a frameless glass walk-in shower, built-in bench, black fixtures and a herringbone wood-look tile wall

why_choose_us.h2: Reasons homeowners near Bethesda pick Boss

items.title: A price that holds
items.text: Selections are made before construction begins, so there are no allowances. The firm puts it plainly: if your project starts at $200,000, it ends at $200,000.

items.title: Two showrooms to shop in person
items.text: See cabinet doors, counters and tile at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue in Bethesda or at 1389 Chain Bridge Road in McLean, by appointment Monday through Saturday.

items.title: Licensed in all three jurisdictions
items.text: Boss holds a Virginia Class A contractor license plus Maryland and Washington, DC contractor licenses. It is bonded and insured, with an A+ BBB rating and NKBA membership.

items.title: A written warranty
items.text: Every project includes a 5-year warranty on structural work and a 1-year warranty on finishes, fixtures, cabinetry, countertops, tile, plumbing, electrical and hardware.

about.h2: Led by architectural designer Talha Gursoy
about.text: Talha Gursoy leads design at Boss Design Center, and the firm's careers page lists its President as Taha A. Gursoy. He holds a Bachelor's and a Master's degree in Architecture and has more than ten years in design-build work, focused on interior design and construction. Homeowners often meet him first. One wrote that at the first visit he did not ask about budget right away but simply listened, and that his renderings matched the finished kitchen. Talha also writes the firm's blog, with plain guides on Virginia permits, fixed-rate contracts and German versus American cabinets.

image.alt: Talha Gursoy, architectural designer and President of Boss Design Center in Bethesda, MD

process.h2: From first visit to final punch list

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: A remodeling planner visits your home, looks at the space and talks through your ideas, budget and timeline. There is no cost and no obligation.

steps.title: Design and 3D rendering
steps.text: The designer measures the existing structure, then presents a photorealistic rendering with a scope budget and projected timeline. This stage typically takes one to two months.

steps.title: Selections and fixed-rate contract
steps.text: You choose cabinets, counters, backsplash, fixtures and paint colors in the showroom. With every detail set, the contract price is fixed.

steps.title: Permits and preparation
steps.text: The team applies for permits, orders materials and introduces your project manager. Expect about four to six weeks from contract to start.

steps.title: Construction and walkthrough
steps.text: Building typically takes three to four months, with weekly in-person meetings and online updates. A full punch list is finished before the job closes.

service_area.h2: Where Boss works in Maryland, Virginia and DC
service_area.text: From the Bethesda showroom, the team remodels homes in Chevy Chase, Potomac, Kensington, Rockville, Silver Spring, Cabin John and nearby Maryland towns. The McLean design campus serves Arlington, Alexandria, Vienna, Great Falls, Fairfax, Falls Church, Reston and out to Leesburg and Ashburn. In the District, project photos on the site come from Georgetown, Kalorama, Cleveland Park, Wesley Heights and Capitol Hill.

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel with Boss cost?
items.a: The firm says its own kitchen projects run $80,000 to $250,000. Your number depends on size, layout changes and the finishes you pick. Because every detail is chosen before construction, the contract is fixed-rate with no allowances, so the price you sign is the price you pay.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: Design and selections typically take one to two months. Permits and ordering add about four to six weeks from contract to start, and construction typically runs three to four months. The firm's own guide puts a full kitchen at about six to eight months from first consultation to finish.

Yes. Your project manager and crew apply for the permits you need and file them with your local jurisdiction. Boss holds contractor licenses in Maryland, Virginia and Washington, DC, including a Virginia Class A license, the top tier, which has no project value limit.

items.q: What warranty comes with the work?
items.a: Each project includes a 5-year warranty on structural work and a 1-year warranty on finishes, fixtures, cabinetry, countertops, tile, plumbing, electrical and hardware. Before the job is called finished, the team works through a full punch list with you and completes every item on it.

items.q: Can I see materials before I commit?
items.a: Yes. The Bethesda showroom at 7220 Wisconsin Avenue, Suite 110, and the McLean design campus at 1389 Chain Bridge Road are open Monday through Saturday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., by appointment. Call (301) 200-9991 to book a time to look at cabinets, counters and tile.

final_cta.h2: See your new kitchen before the first wall comes down
final_cta.text: Call the Bethesda showroom to book a free in-home consultation and start on your rendering.
